rule.statement: On when (1) the settled-correct lower95 meets the site's bar (0.95; J3: its recorded final-route bar), (2) the accuracy of the site with Jev on is not below the incumbent's by more than 0.02 on the same cases, (3) Jev is faster by median latency, or cheaper per call, or the site with Jev on is more accurate, and (4) no constraint the site's record adds is broken; otherwise the original path stays.
rule.siteConditions: plan 2026-10-06 section 4.1, J4: no false notice on real sentences of non-clinical capability reports

measuredOn: A development host in Taipei, where both providers answer a bare request in about 0.16 s. The production host is in Beijing: TypeSafe is reached there in 0.5 to 0.6 s (plan 2026-10-06 section 0), and a 325-token Jev request took 0.33 to 1.24 s on 2026-10-07 (4 requests, privateEvidence latency-production-host.json). Latency here compares the two paths on one network; it is not the production figure.
incumbentCostBasis: List prices (peak) from the reference price list on the tokens the provider reported. A repeated run of identical prompts is partly served from DeepSeek's prompt cache and costs less than a first call; production questions are new, so the first pass of a site is the representative one.

decision.summary: Stays on. Both passes qualify (127 of 127 and 126 of 126 settled answers right, lower95 0.977), no non-clinical sentence drew a false notice (0 of 75), and the site is more accurate than the pattern it replaced.

notes.incumbent: Before Jev a delivered report carried no register notice. The frozen pattern that stood beside J4 as a drift comparator (reportRegisterJudge.mjs) is scored here as the incumbent: it costs nothing and takes no time, and is right on 111 of 140 labelled lines.
notes.benefit: More accurate than the pattern on the same 140 lines (Jev 140 of 140 with its answers settled and the rest left as no notice, against 111), which is the benefit; the pattern is free and instant, so Jev is neither faster nor cheaper than it.
notes.driftBaseline: The pin's drift baseline is 0.80, read from production on 2026-10-10 (2,855 comparisons against the pattern, daily agreement 0.811 and 0.804 once the site had settled); it is a statement about agreement with the pattern, not about accuracy.
